articles.headline: US Treasuries Hold Losses After Core CPI Tops Estimates on Inflation Worries
articles.summary: The April 2026 CPI report released today showed consumer prices rising 3.8% year-over-year, with core CPI up 2.8%, both exceeding economist estimates. Treasury yields rose 2-3 basis points across maturities, with 30-year yields hovering near 5%, and swaps traders now pricing in a ~70% chance of a Fed rate hike by April 2027. The persistently elevated inflation — driven largely by war-related energy price spikes from the Iran conflict — has effectively killed any near-term prospect for Fed rate cuts, locking borrowing costs at elevated levels. For IE industrial brokers, this means cap rate compression remains off the table and buyer financing costs stay high, continuing to suppress investment sales activity and complicating deal underwriting.

articles.headline: US CPI Report April 2026: Key Takeaways on Inflation, Consumer Price Index
articles.summary: Bloomberg's live coverage and key takeaways on today's April 2026 CPI release showed all-items inflation at 3.8% YoY, accelerating from March's 3.3%, driven by surging gasoline and shelter costs tied to the Iran War energy shock. The report notes record-low consumer sentiment and the Fed's preferred PCE gauge had already accelerated to 3.5% headline in March. The data virtually ensures no Fed rate cuts in 2026 and increases the probability of a rate hike. For Southern California industrial brokers, persistent inflation raises tenant operating costs, compresses tenant affordability for rent increases, and keeps the bid-ask gap between buyers and sellers wide.

articles.headline: Inland Empire Manufacturing Building Sells to Investor
articles.summary: Proficio Realty LLC acquired a 17,767-square-foot industrial manufacturing building at 255 Glider Circle in Corona, California from Mark J. & Ronda L. Haupert for $5.3 million, or $298 per square foot. The deal reflects continued investor appetite for smaller, functional manufacturing assets in the western Inland Empire despite broader market headwinds. At $298/SF, this transaction provides a meaningful pricing data point for mid-size owner-user and investor activity in the Corona/Riverside corridor. IE brokers should note that smaller manufacturing buildings continue to transact at premium per-square-foot pricing compared to larger big-box logistics space currently being pressured by elevated vacancies.

articles.headline: Port of Los Angeles Chief Says Shipping Won't Normalize Without Lasting Hormuz Stability
articles.summary: Port of LA Executive Director Gene Seroka stated there is a 'lack of confidence in the region, with only a handful of ships moving through the Strait compared to the usual 100,' warning that normalization requires a sustained, proven peace agreement. Despite this, the Port of LA processed 460,020 TEUs in April — its second-best April on record, up 1.5% YoY — largely on pre-conflict front-loading momentum. Seroka flagged that diesel prices are up 50% at the port, squeezing the roughly 1,200 small trucking companies operating in and out of the facility. For IE industrial brokers, the port disruption is a double-edged signal: near-term cargo volume may hold, but rising freight and fuel costs are pressuring logistics tenants' operating margins and could trigger lease renegotiations or space consolidations.

articles.headline: Ships at LA's Ports Face a Fuel Shock That's Shaking the Economy
articles.summary: Cargo ships at the Ports of LA and Long Beach are facing fuel costs nearly 20% higher than other major global ports, as the Strait of Hormuz closure since late February has cut off California's average 200,000 barrels per day of Persian Gulf oil imports. The average price of very low-sulfur fuel oil has surged 70% to $925 per metric ton globally since the Iran War started, with fuel now representing 25% of total voyage costs from Asia to Los Angeles. Shipping majors including Hapag-Lloyd, Maersk, and Amazon are passing costs onto shippers, consumers, and importers via surcharges. For IE industrial brokers and tenants, rising freight costs are reducing the volume and profitability of goods flowing through SoCal warehouses, potentially softening warehouse demand from import-dependent distributors and retailers.

articles.headline: BofA Delays Fed Rate-Cut Forecast Into 2027
articles.summary: Bank of America Global Research now forecasts no Fed rate cuts in 2026, pushing its first expected cut to July 2027, citing elevated inflation driven by the Iran War energy shock. The Fed held its benchmark rate steady at 3.50%–3.75% at its April 29 meeting in an unusually divisive 8–4 vote, the closest split since 1992. March PCE came in at 3.5% headline and 3.2% core — well above the Fed's 2% target — with Nationwide economists projecting inflation could peak near 4.5% this summer. For IE industrial brokers, a prolonged higher-rate environment means continued cap rate pressure, slower investment sales volumes, and financing challenges for buyers of larger industrial assets in the $20M–$100M+ range.

articles.headline: He's on a Mission to Find Opportunities in Southern California's Choppy Industrial Market
articles.summary: Lincoln Property Company executive Sean Perrier says Southern California industrial demand is 'recalibrating' rather than collapsing, with the biggest challenge being identifying true market rents amid ongoing uncertainty. Lincoln has assembled a cluster of ~10 industrial buildings near Ontario, ranging from 50,000 to 250,000 SF, targeting infill assets with stabilized cash flow and value-add upside in the IE's deep logistics corridor. Perrier expects shrinking new supply pipelines to eventually make landowners more willing sellers, opening doors for new industrial development in undersupplied IE pockets. For local brokers, this signals that well-capitalized institutional players are actively hunting for deals in the IE, suggesting the investment market may be closer to a floor than the elevated vacancy rate implies.

articles.headline: JLL Arranges $26M Bridge Financing for Industrial Outdoor Storage Facility in Anaheim
articles.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged $26 million in bridge financing for a 7.75-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) facility at 1477 N. Jefferson St. in Anaheim for borrower North Palisade Partners. The deal was structured as a non-recourse, three-year floating-rate loan by Senior Director Peter Thompson, Associate Kyle White, and Analyst Nick Englhard. The Class A property spans approximately 337,590 square feet of industrial outdoor storage. For Orange County and LA Basin industrial brokers, this transaction highlights growing institutional and lender interest in IOS assets as an industrial sub-sector, reflecting strong demand for truck parking, container storage, and fleet maintenance facilities near the region's port gateway.

articles.headline: AI Expected to Boost Demand for US Industrial, Office, Retail Space by 12% in Next Decade
articles.summary: A new Cushman & Wakefield report projects AI-driven productivity gains will generate approximately 330 million square feet of additional U.S. commercial real estate demand over the next decade — with industrial leading at +298.5 million square feet (+13.3%). The demand boost is driven by AI's impact on inventory management, logistics automation, and warehousing needs for automated supply chains, and notably excludes data centers themselves. The baseline scenario (50% probability) assumes gradual AI adoption through 2035, creating a bigger economy that demands more space rather than less. For IE industrial brokers, this is a bullish long-term structural signal: automated logistics and manufacturing facilities will drive demand for modern, power-intensive industrial space — exactly the type of product being developed in the Inland Empire.

articles.headline: EQT to Buy Majority Stake in 12 Cold Storage Warehouses Through Americold Deal
articles.summary: Americold Realty Trust (NYSE: COLD) and EQT announced a $1.3 billion joint venture, with EQT acquiring a 70% stake in 12 U.S. cold storage warehouses totaling ~124 million cubic feet and 400,000+ pallet positions, while Americold retains 30% and day-to-day management. Americold expects ~$1.1 billion in net cash proceeds to pay down debt, helping repair a balance sheet stressed by occupancy declines and overbuilding in the cold storage sector. The deal is expected to close in Q3 2026 and is positioned as a platform for future cold storage development. For SoCal industrial brokers, this large-scale cold storage consolidation reinforces investor conviction in temperature-controlled logistics infrastructure — an increasingly relevant sub-sector given SoCal's role in food distribution near the nation's largest ports.

articles.headline: Global Net Lease To Acquire Modiv Industrial REIT In $535M Deal
articles.summary: Global Net Lease (NYSE: GNL) agreed to acquire Modiv Industrial (NYSE: MDV) — the only public REIT exclusively focused on industrial manufacturing real estate — in a $535 million all-stock deal at a 17% premium. Modiv owns 42 properties in 14 states, with a majority in California, featuring a weighted average lease term of 15 years and 2.4% annual rent escalations. The transaction is expected to be immediately 4% accretive to GNL's AFFO per share and is expected to close in Q3 2026. For IE industrial brokers, this consolidation confirms that net-leased industrial manufacturing assets — especially California-heavy portfolios — continue to attract institutional premium pricing, signaling durable demand for mission-critical industrial real estate even amid broader market softness.

articles.headline: Inland Empire Industrial Slump Deepens, But Brokers Say Rebound May Be Near
articles.summary: The Inland Empire's industrial vacancy rate reached 7.8% in Q1 2026 with negative net absorption of 4.7 million SF, driven by four 1 million+ SF move-outs as tenants consolidated or relocated, per CBRE. However, the construction pipeline collapsed to just 102,000 SF delivered in Q1 2026, down sharply from nearly 2 million SF in Q1 2025, leading brokers to forecast that vacancy has likely peaked or is near its peak. Colliers tracked IE West rents at $1.10/SF and IE East at $0.90/SF, with a lack of consensus on whether rents have further to fall complicating transaction pricing. For IE brokers, the critical takeaway is that the supply-side problem is essentially resolved — the risk of further vacancy increases from new deliveries is minimal, setting the stage for gradual market recovery in late 2026 or 2027.

articles.headline: Honda Remains Mum on Future of Ontario EV Plant Amid Speculation It's Been Shelved
articles.summary: Development remains stalled on Honda's planned $15 billion electric vehicle and battery manufacturing complex in Alliston, Ontario, after construction ceased in May 2025 as EV demand cratered — with US EV sales down 28% YoY in Q1 2026 following the expiration of federal tax credits. Honda has recalibrated its North American strategy to focus on hybrid vehicles rather than EVs, taking a massive 2.5 trillion yen ($15.7B) writedown and reporting its first annual loss in nearly 70 years. While the Ontario plant is referenced above, CoStar had previously reported on Honda's Ontario, California logistics/manufacturing presence and how EV strategy shifts broadly affect Southern California's advanced manufacturing and supplier ecosystem. For IE industrial brokers, the collapse of EV manufacturing buildout signals reduced demand from EV-supply-chain tenants that had been expected to drive specialized manufacturing leasing activity.

articles.headline: Commercial Mortgage Originations Jump 52% in Q1 2026, Industrial Leads Gains
articles.summary: Commercial and multifamily mortgage loan originations were 52% higher in Q1 2026 compared to a year earlier, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association's Quarterly Survey, with increases across healthcare, retail, hotel, and industrial properties leading the overall lending volume jump. This marks a significant acceleration in CRE debt market activity despite elevated interest rates and geopolitical uncertainty, suggesting lenders are becoming more comfortable underwriting stabilized industrial assets. The surge in originations provides new financing pathways for industrial property owners in Southern California looking to refinance maturing loans or fund acquisitions. For IE brokers, improved lending conditions could help unlock pent-up deal flow as more buyers can access capital at workable terms.

articles.headline: Wall Street Banks Push Back Fed Rate Cut Forecasts After Strong Jobs Data
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs and Bank of America have both pushed back their Federal Reserve rate-cut forecasts following a stronger-than-expected April jobs report (115,000 payrolls added vs. 65,000 forecast) and persistently elevated inflation. BofA now expects no rate cuts in 2026, with the first two 25bp cuts in July and September 2027, while Goldman Sachs moved its first-cut call to December 2026. The Fed held rates steady at 3.50–3.75% at its April 29 meeting in an unusually divisive 8–4 vote, the closest since 1992, with the Iran war driving energy prices higher. For IE industrial brokers, this 'higher-for-longer' rate environment means continued cap rate pressure, tighter deal financing, and buyers remaining cautious — further delaying investment sales transaction velocity in SoCal industrial markets.

articles.headline: BofA Delays Fed Rate-Cut Forecast Into 2027
articles.summary: Bank of America's head of U.S. economics Aditya Bhave stated 'the data simply don't warrant cuts this year,' as core inflation is 'too high and moving up,' with the Cleveland Fed forecasting CPI hitting 3.89% for May. The Iran war has driven energy prices sharply higher, with headline PCE accelerating to 3.5% year-over-year and core PCE at 3.2% as of March 2026. The April CPI report — expected to show 3.7% headline inflation — was released May 12, adding further pressure on the Fed. IE industrial brokers should note that stalled rate relief will continue to suppress investment sales volume and widen the bid-ask spread between buyers and sellers in the SoCal industrial market through at least year-end.

articles.headline: Port of Los Angeles Posts Second-Best April on Record Amid Strong Import Demand
articles.summary: The Port of Los Angeles processed 890,861 TEUs in April 2026, up 5.7% year-over-year, marking the second-best April on record despite ongoing tariff and trade policy uncertainty. Loaded imports totaled 459,825 TEUs, a 5% increase year-over-year and 21% higher than March. Executive Director Gene Seroka noted the next wave of back-to-school and early holiday merchandise is already building in Asia. For Inland Empire industrial brokers, this robust port activity is a leading indicator of near-term warehouse demand, as increased import volumes historically translate to higher leasing activity in the IE's logistics corridors within 60–90 days.

articles.headline: JLL Secures $26M Bridge Financing for Anaheim Industrial Outdoor Storage Facility
articles.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged $26 million in bridge financing for a 7.75-acre, Class A industrial outdoor storage (IOS) facility at 1477 N. Jefferson St. in Anaheim, Orange County. The non-recourse, three-year, floating-rate loan was secured on behalf of borrower North Palisade Partners by JLL's Peter Thompson, Kyle White, and Nick Englhard. The property occupies 337,590 square feet in one of Southern California's most supply-constrained industrial submarkets. This deal highlights the continued institutional appetite for IOS assets in infill Orange County locations, where scarcity of available land supports premium valuations and strong lender interest even in a high-rate environment.

articles.headline: Global Net Lease to Acquire Modiv Industrial in $535 Million All-Stock Transaction
articles.summary: Global Net Lease (NYSE: GNL) announced a definitive merger agreement to acquire Modiv Industrial (NYSE: MDV) in an all-stock deal valued at approximately $535 million, representing a 17% premium to Modiv's May 1 closing price. Modiv's portfolio includes 42 properties with a 15-year weighted-average lease term, 45% investment-grade tenants, and 2.4% annual rent escalations, with California properties in the mix. The deal is expected to be 4% accretive to GNL's AFFO per share and is structured to be leverage-neutral, with closing expected in Q3 2026. For SoCal industrial brokers, this consolidation signals continued institutional demand for net-leased industrial assets with long-term, credit-quality tenants — a strategy increasingly favored as the market resets from peak valuations.

articles.headline: Lincoln Property Raises $280M Cornerstone Close for $1B Logistics Fund II
articles.summary: Lincoln Property Company announced the cornerstone close of Lincoln Logistics Fund II with $280 million in capital commitments from long-term institutional investors including U.S. public pension plans, representing nearly one-third of the fund's $1 billion target. The value-add fund will primarily target last-mile and multi-tenant industrial investments across the U.S., with up to 35% allocated to development, and has already acquired one asset with two more awarded. Lincoln has been actively expanding in Southern California, including its acquisition of Inland Empire industrial assets near Ontario and its hire of Sean Perrier specifically to source SoCal deals. IE industrial brokers should track Lincoln as a well-capitalized active buyer targeting infill and value-add assets in the current market dislocation.

articles.headline: Columbia Container Lines Inks $13.6M, 68-Month Industrial Lease in Fullerton
articles.summary: The Klabin Company/CORFAC International represented Columbia Container Lines LAX, Inc. in a 68-month lease for a 156,096-square-foot industrial property at 691-701 Burning Tree Road in Fullerton, Orange County, valued at more than $13.6 million. Tyler Rollema, SIOR, and Matt Stringfellow, SIOR, of The Klabin Company represented the tenant, which is relocating and expanding from its previous location. The deal reflects continued demand from port-adjacent logistics users in Orange County's tight industrial market. For brokers, this lease underscores that port-proximate users like container lines are still actively seeking and committing to longer-term leases in OC's infill industrial corridors despite broader market softness.

articles.headline: Rexford Industrial Q1 2026 Beats EPS Forecast, Reports Record Leasing Activity, Raises Full-Year Guidance
articles.summary: Rexford Industrial Realty (NYSE: REXR), the dominant infill SoCal industrial REIT, reported Q1 2026 EPS of $0.38, beating the $0.27 consensus estimate by 40.74%, with Core FFO of $139.8 million ($0.61/share) and revenue of $245.08 million. The company executed a record 4.1 million square feet of leases in Q1 and raised its full-year 2026 Core FFO per share guidance, while authorizing a $500 million share repurchase program. Rexford's portfolio of 414 properties totaling 50.4 million rentable square feet remained heavily occupied, with CEO Howard Schwimmer citing 'record leasing activity and strategic capital recycling' in a supply-constrained market. For IE and SoCal industrial brokers, Rexford's outperformance signals that infill assets with genuine scarcity continue to command premium performance even as the broader market faces headwinds.

articles.headline: Southern California Industrial Landlords Face Biggest U.S. Leasing Drop; IE Vacancy Hits 9%
articles.summary: Southern California industrial landlords are contending with some of the steepest occupancy losses in the U.S., with Inland Empire tenants vacating 4 million square feet more than they moved into in a recent quarter — among the worst of any U.S. market. Industrial rents in the IE have fallen 3.4% in the past year and remain 25% below the 2023 peak, with major retailers like Forever 21, Kohl's, Harbor Freight Tools, and Home Depot giving back large spaces. Inland Empire East faces particularly severe pressure, with availability exceeding 20% in the 250,000–500,000 SF range, though cross-dock terminals and trailer yards see steadier demand. Brokers should expect landlords to offer meaningful concessions — free rent, flexible lease terms, and TI packages — to attract and retain tenants, especially in large-format spaces in the eastern IE.

articles.headline: Inland Empire Industrial Overall Vacancy Rises to 8.9% in Q1 2026, Above 10-Year Average
articles.summary: The Inland Empire industrial overall vacancy rate increased 10 basis points quarter-over-quarter to 8.9% and rose 40 basis points year-over-year in Q1 2026, remaining well above the 10-year average of 4.0% according to Cushman & Wakefield's latest MarketBeat. The broader availability rate, which includes sublease space, stood at 13.1% and remained stagnant, suggesting limited near-term relief for landlords. Despite elevated vacancies, market sentiment is gradually improving as new construction deliveries slow materially, pointing toward a potential stabilization trajectory in 2026. IE industrial brokers should note that tenants hold significant negotiating leverage, particularly in Class A big-box space, while infill and smaller-bay assets are showing more resilient fundamentals.

articles.headline: CoStar Expects U.S. Industrial Vacancy to Peak in 2026; Rent Growth to Remain Near +1.0%
articles.summary: CoStar's revised industrial forecast projects the national vacancy rate will rise from 7.5% to 7.8% by year-end 2026 before declining through 2027, with average annual rent growth decelerating to approximately +1.0% before reaccelerating to +2.8% by end of 2027. The modest near-term vacancy increase is driven by ongoing supply additions and continued space givebacks, with West Coast port markets — including Southern California — expected to underperform due to reduced demand tied to the ongoing trade war. CoStar notes that if tariffs remain elevated and consumer spending weakens further, industrial vacancy could reach 8–9% nationally, creating a more significant drag on rents. For IE brokers, the forecast implies the market correction is not yet over, but the trajectory toward stabilization in late 2026 may present early mover acquisition opportunities.

articles.headline: Port of LA's April Cargo Surge Points to 'Next Wave' of Back-to-School Imports Already Building in Asia
articles.summary: Through the first four months of 2026, the Port of Los Angeles has handled 3,279,704 TEUs, running 2% ahead of its five-year average for the period despite being 2% below last year's front-loaded pace. Executive Director Gene Seroka reported that retailers and manufacturers are continuing to move goods despite trade uncertainty, and confirmed that back-to-school and early holiday merchandise sourcing activity is already underway in Asia. The port's April performance — the highest cargo volume since last August — signals that consumer demand remains resilient even amid tariff headwinds and the Iran war's energy price impacts. For Inland Empire warehouse brokers, near-term leasing demand from logistics operators handling seasonal import surges could pick up meaningfully through Q3 2026 in proximity to the San Pedro Bay port complex.

articles.headline: BofA Drops Blunt Warning About Fed Rate Cuts for Remainder of 2026
articles.summary: Bank of America Global Research has revised its Fed rate-cut forecast, now expecting no cuts in 2026 and the next reductions not until July and September 2027. BofA cites the 11-week Iran War's energy price shock and a stronger-than-expected April jobs report (115,000 nonfarm payrolls, unemployment steady at 4.3%) as justification. The Fed held rates at 3.50%–3.75% in an historic 8-4 vote at its April 29 meeting. For IE industrial brokers, prolonged elevated rates directly constrain investment sales, widen bid-ask spreads, and pressure leveraged buyers — particularly relevant as the IE market continues to work through vacancy normalization.

articles.headline: Top Industrial Leases Recognized for Inland Empire — Tireco, Medline and Unis Among Q1 Winners
articles.summary: CoStar's Power Broker Quarterly Deals recognition highlights the top Q1 2026 industrial leases in the Inland Empire, with prominent deals signed by Tireco, Medline, and Unis — all negotiated by CBRE dealmakers. The recognition signals that despite elevated vacancy rates, significant leasing activity continued in Q1 2026 from industrial, logistics, and distribution tenants. The Inland Empire overall vacancy rate rose to 8.9% in Q1 2026 per Cushman & Wakefield data, yet large-tenant demand from health, auto parts, and logistics sectors remains active. IE industrial brokers should note that well-located, functional space is still transacting, with CBRE capturing dominant market share on major deals.

articles.headline: Goodman Launches Leasing at 1.6M-SF Inland Empire West Logistics Campus
articles.summary: Goodman has launched leasing at Goodman Logistics Center Rancho Cucamonga, described as the largest contiguous logistics campus currently available in the Inland Empire West, totaling 1.6 million square feet across two buildings with move-in readiness expected in Q3 2026. Goodman CEO Anthony Rozic cited continued double-digit e-commerce growth and demand for last-mile delivery capabilities serving 18 million people in Greater Los Angeles as the strategic rationale. The campus's Rancho Cucamonga location provides direct access to more than 18 million consumers across Greater LA. For IE brokers, this represents a major new supply addition entering the market just as the IE West vacancy stabilizes — tenant absorption of this campus will be a key indicator of market health in H2 2026.

articles.headline: JLL Capital Markets Arranges $26M Bridge Financing for Anaheim Industrial Outdoor Storage Facility
articles.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged $26 million in bridge financing for a 7.75-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) facility at 1477 N. Jefferson St. in Anaheim, Orange County, on behalf of borrower North Palisade Partners. The non-recourse, three-year, floating-rate loan was secured by JLL's Peter Thompson, Kyle White, and Nick Englhard. The Class A IOS property spans 337,590 square feet in one of Southern California's tightest infill logistics submarkets. For IE/OC industrial brokers, this transaction highlights the continued capital availability for well-located IOS assets despite the broader financing challenges — and signals that lenders remain active in Orange County's supply-constrained industrial market.

articles.headline: Columbia Container Lines Inks $13.6M, 156,096-SF Industrial Lease in Fullerton
articles.summary: The Klabin Company/CORFAC International represented Columbia Container Lines LAX, Inc. in a 68-month lease for a 156,096-square-foot industrial property at 691-701 Burning Tree Road in Fullerton, valued at more than $13.6 million. The shipping company is relocating and expanding from its prior location, with Tyler Rollema, SIOR, and Matt Stringfellow, SIOR, of The Klabin Company representing the tenant. This Orange County industrial lease transaction represents one of the larger recent deals in the OC market, demonstrating ongoing demand from port-adjacent logistics and container shipping users. For IE/OC brokers, the deal underscores that shipping and container companies continue to seek functional industrial space in infill OC locations despite broader market softness.

articles.headline: Lincoln Property Closes $280M Cornerstone for Lincoln Logistics Fund II Targeting Last-Mile Industrial
articles.summary: Lincoln Property Company announced the cornerstone close of Lincoln Logistics Fund II with $280 million in capital commitments, representing nearly one-third of the fund's $1 billion target, with support from two U.S. public pension plans. The fund will primarily target last-mile and multi-tenant industrial investments across the U.S. This capital raise directly ties to Lincoln's SoCal industrial strategy, which includes a cluster of roughly 10 industrial buildings near Ontario in the Inland Empire. For IE industrial brokers, this signals that major institutional capital is being deployed specifically for infill, last-mile industrial assets in the region — a potential driver of increased acquisition activity and investment sales volume in 2026.

articles.headline: Commercial and Multifamily Mortgage Originations Surge 52% in Q1 2026
articles.summary: The Mortgage Bankers Association's Q1 2026 survey shows commercial and multifamily mortgage loan originations were 52% higher than the same period a year ago, led by increases in healthcare, retail, hotel, and industrial property lending. The data points to improving financing conditions in early 2026 even as the broader rate environment remains elevated. This surge in originations suggests lenders are more willing to engage with industrial transactions as market conditions stabilize. For IE industrial brokers, the lending recovery is a meaningful signal that deal velocity could improve in 2026 — particularly for stabilized, well-leased industrial assets which remain lenders' preferred collateral.

articles.headline: Port of Long Beach Outpaces Rivals as Tariffs and Iran War Cloud Outlook
articles.summary: The Port of Long Beach processed 774,935 TEUs in March 2026, down 5.2% year-over-year against a record 2025 baseline, while remaining the busiest seaport in the U.S. through Q1. Imports slipped 1.6% while the port cited tariff uncertainty, inflation, and rising fuel costs tied to the Iran conflict as key headwinds. Port CEO Noel Hacegaba noted that ship rerouting around conflict zones lengthens routes and raises costs, which ultimately impact consumers. For IE industrial brokers, slowing port volumes are a leading indicator of reduced warehouse demand from importers and logistics tenants — directly impacting absorption rates and lease renewal decisions across the Inland Empire's distribution market.

articles.headline: Honda Shelves $11 Billion Canadian EV Plant as Slowing US Demand Forces Strategy Pivot
articles.summary: Honda has indefinitely shelved its $15 billion CAD EV and battery manufacturing complex in Ontario, Canada, with construction halted since May 2025 amid flagging U.S. EV demand — which fell 28% year-over-year in Q1 2026 after federal tax credits expired. Honda is recalibrating its North American strategy toward hybrid vehicles and took a $15.7 billion writedown on its EV business in its first annual loss as a public company in nearly 70 years. The move signals a broader auto industry retreat from EV investment driven by tariffs, policy shifts, and weak consumer demand. For IE industrial brokers, this reinforces that EV-related industrial demand (battery plants, parts distribution) remains volatile — but the hybrid pivot may sustain demand for traditional auto parts warehousing and logistics space in the region.

articles.headline: Inland Empire Industrial Vacancy Rises to 8.9% in Q1 2026 as Market Continues Digestion Phase
articles.summary: Cushman & Wakefield's Q1 2026 Inland Empire MarketBeat reports the overall vacancy rate increased to 8.9%, rising 10 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 40 bps year-over-year — well above the 10-year average of 4.0%. The industrial-specific vacancy rate reached 8.5% in Q1 2026, up 50 bps quarter-over-quarter. Sublease availability has remained stagnant at elevated levels, though market sentiment is gradually improving. For IE industrial brokers, the continued vacancy climb signals that tenants still hold leverage in lease negotiations, but the slowing pace of new construction deliveries may help the market stabilize by year-end as the supply pipeline thins significantly.

articles.headline: Fed Official Warns Higher Inflation May Delay Rate Cuts, Hike Back on Table
articles.summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago President Austan Goolsbee stated on Bloomberg Television that all interest-rate policy options — including a rate hike — are on the table, citing inflation concerns driven by the Iran War energy shock. The March 2026 PCE showed headline inflation accelerating to 3.5% year-over-year (up from 2.8% in February) while core PCE rose to 3.2%. Economists at Nationwide expect inflation to peak near 4.5% this summer — more than double the Fed's 2% target. For IE industrial brokers, the possibility of rate hikes rather than cuts fundamentally changes the investment calculus for clients evaluating acquisitions, refinancings, or development decisions in 2026.

articles.headline: CPI Surge Squeezes US Voters Already Facing High Fuel, Food Prices
articles.summary: The April CPI came in at 3.8% year-over-year — the highest since May 2023 — driven by a 3.8% monthly energy spike and 0.5% food increase, both tied to the ongoing Iran war and Strait of Hormuz blockade. Real wages fell 0.3% annually, the first such drop since 2023, signaling consumer spending headwinds. For IE industrial brokers, this confirms that tenants in consumer goods, retail, and 3PL sectors will remain cautious about committing to new long-term leases. Elevated inflation also reinforces the 'higher for longer' rate environment, continuing to compress deal velocity and keeping cap rate expansion pressure on industrial valuations.

articles.headline: Markets Raise Chances for a Fed Rate Hike Following Hot Inflation Report
articles.summary: Following the hotter-than-expected April CPI report, market pricing moved to virtually eliminate any chance of a Fed rate cut through the end of 2027 while pricing in a 37% probability of a rate increase before year-end. The Fed held rates at 3.50%-3.75% at its April 29 meeting in an unusually divisive 8-4 vote — the most divided FOMC since October 1992. For IE industrial brokers, this 'higher for longer' — or potentially 'even higher' — rate environment is a direct headwind to tenant decision-making and investor underwriting. Expect continued tenant hesitation on large-format leases and persistent price discovery challenges in investment sales.

articles.headline: CPI Inflation April 2026: Prices Rose 3.8% Annually
articles.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported the April CPI rose 0.6% month-over-month and 3.8% year-over-year, with energy prices jumping 3.8% in April alone and food prices up 0.5%. Core CPI rose 0.4% monthly and 2.8% annually, with shelter rising 0.6% — its biggest monthly gain since September 2023. CNBC noted persistent increases in transportation and warehousing indexes as a sign the price shock is spreading beyond energy. For IE industrial brokers, inflationary pressure on operating costs — diesel, insurance, labor — squeezes tenant margins, accelerating downsizing or sublease decisions and adding to the already elevated 278 million SF of sublease inventory nationally.

articles.headline: Shipping Industry Fears Fuel Shortages as Iran War Squeezes Bunker Fuel Supply
articles.summary: The Iran war's closure of the Strait of Hormuz has choked off bunker fuel supply powering the global maritime industry, with the daily cost to global shipping estimated at nearly $400 million. Bunker fuel shortages feed through to shipping costs quickly, and the cumulative effect ripples across supply chains to influence consumer prices across a broad range of sectors. For IE industrial brokers, this is a critical dual-threat: higher shipping costs slow import volumes through the Ports of LA and Long Beach, reducing warehouse demand from importers and 3PLs; simultaneously, fuel surcharges from Amazon, FedEx, and USPS signal that logistics occupiers are absorbing severe cost pressures that could trigger lease downsizing or consolidations.

articles.headline: Ships at LA's Ports Face a Fuel Shock That's Shaking the Economy
articles.summary: Cargo ships at the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach are facing extreme fuel costs, with very low-sulfur fuel oil nearly 88% more expensive at the LA/LB complex than pre-war levels — rising to $1,080 per metric ton versus a global average of $925. Port of LA activity was down 3% year-over-year in March while Long Beach handled 774,935 containers, though operations have not dramatically slowed. For IE industrial brokers, higher shipping fuel costs directly translate to reduced import volumes over time, diminishing the key demand driver for Inland Empire warehouse space. Amazon's 3.5% fuel surcharge and USPS's 8% package fee signal that e-commerce fulfillment operators — the backbone of IE demand — are under serious cost pressure.

articles.headline: Top Industrial Leases Recognized for Inland Empire
articles.summary: CoStar's Q1 2026 Power Broker Quarterly Deals recognized prominent industrial leases signed by Tireco, Medline, and Unis — all brokered by top CBRE dealmakers — as among the most significant first-quarter industrial transactions in the Inland Empire. The recognition signals that despite elevated 9% vacancy, large-format lease deals are still being executed by experienced tenant representation teams. For IE industrial brokers, these transactions validate that institutional-quality tenants in tire distribution (Tireco), medical supplies (Medline), and logistics (Unis) remain active — but competition for these high-profile tenants is intensifying among top brokerage houses, making local expertise and relationships more critical than ever.

articles.headline: BGO and Sun Life's Industrial Platform Eyes Expansion Ahead of Connect Los Angeles 2026
articles.summary: BGO and its parent Sun Life — which recently combined with multifamily operator Bell Partners — is positioning its industrial platform for expanded Southern California investment activity ahead of the Connect Los Angeles 2026 conference on May 28. BGO's industrial strategy is focused on speculative and build-to-suit development, with the fund targeting opportunities in markets like Los Angeles and the Inland Empire. For IE industrial brokers, BGO's continued presence signals that institutional capital remains committed to SoCal industrial even amid the market correction, though focus is shifting to build-to-suit and income-producing value-add versus speculative big-box. The Connect LA event itself will be a key gathering for deal-making intelligence.

articles.headline: BofA Delays Fed Rate-Cut Forecast Into 2027 After Hot Jobs and Inflation Data
articles.summary: Bank of America Global Research now expects the Fed to remain on hold for all of 2026, delaying its rate-cut forecast to July and September 2027. The shift follows the April jobs surprise — nonfarm payrolls rose 115,000 after a strong March — combined with headline PCE inflation accelerating to 3.5% year-over-year in March, driven by energy costs from the Iran war. BofA's head of U.S. economics stated the data simply does not warrant cuts this year, with core inflation too high and moving up. For IE industrial brokers, no rate relief in 2026 means construction financing remains expensive, keeping speculative development suppressed — a dynamic that ultimately benefits vacancy absorption timelines but continues to freeze investment sales activity.

articles.headline: Inland Empire Industrial Vacancy Rate Rises to 8.5%-8.9% in Q1 2026 as Market Seeks Stabilization
articles.summary: Cushman & Wakefield's Q1 2026 Inland Empire MarketBeat reports the overall vacancy rate increased to 8.9%, up 10 basis points quarter-over-quarter and 40 bps year-over-year, while the industrial-specific vacancy rose to 8.5% — rising 50 bps quarter-over-quarter and remaining well above the 10-year average of 4.0%. Despite the elevated vacancy, the report signals that peak vacancy may be in the rearview mirror as demand holds and supply slows. For IE industrial brokers, this data confirms the market is in a tenant-favorable environment but approaching an inflection point — a window of opportunity to help tenants lock in favorable lease terms while advising landlords on competitive concession packages to drive absorption before the market tightens.

articles.headline: US Industrial Leasing Surges 17.8% in Q1 2026 as Supply Chain Shifts Drive Demand
articles.summary: JLL's Q1 2026 U.S. Industrial Market Dynamics Report found national industrial leasing activity jumped 17.8% year-over-year, with 145 million SF of leases executed — 71.6% representing new leases rather than renewals. Asking rates stayed modestly positive, up 0.8% annually to $10.34 per SF nationally, while average direct asking rates for mega-box warehouses rose 14.5% annually. The leasing strength was driven by supply chain diversification, nearshoring manufacturing, and demand for modern logistics facilities. For IE industrial brokers, this national trend contrasts with SoCal's softer dynamics — tenants with flexibility are increasingly considering IE alternatives to more expensive coastal markets, particularly for large-format distribution.

articles.headline: GlobeSt: Large Banks Ease Lending Standards While Construction Lending Weakens Amid Higher Costs
articles.summary: GlobeSt reported that large banks are beginning to ease lending standards for commercial real estate, offering a glimmer of improvement for deal financing, while construction lending remains weak amid persistently higher costs. This bifurcation reflects lenders' preference for income-producing assets over speculative development in the current high-rate environment. For IE industrial brokers, easing standards on acquisition financing — even marginally — could unlock some stalled investment sales on stabilized, leased IE industrial properties. However, the weakness in construction lending reinforces that new speculative development will remain suppressed, which long-term supports vacancy absorption and eventual rent recovery in the Inland Empire.

articles.headline: CPI Inflation April 2026: Prices Rose 3.8% Annually
articles.summary: The April 2026 Consumer Price Index rose 3.8% year-over-year — the highest annual rate since May 2023 — driven by a 3.8% surge in energy prices tied to the ongoing Iran war, which accounted for over 40% of the monthly gain. Core CPI (ex-food and energy) came in at +0.4% MoM and +2.8% YoY, exceeding expectations. Real average hourly wages fell 0.3% annually, compressing consumer purchasing power. For IE industrial brokers, this hot inflation print virtually eliminates any prospect of Fed rate cuts in 2026, keeping commercial borrowing costs elevated and further chilling investment sales and refinancing activity in Southern California industrial properties.

articles.headline: BofA Delays Fed Rate-Cut Forecast Into 2027
articles.summary: Bank of America Global Research now expects the Federal Reserve to keep rates on hold for the remainder of 2026, with two 25bp cuts not occurring until July and September 2027 — a sharp revision from its prior forecast of September 2026. The call is driven by elevated inflation (headline PCE at 3.5% YoY, core PCE at 3.2%), a stronger-than-expected April jobs report (+115,000 nonfarm payrolls), and energy price shocks from the Iran war. Goldman Sachs similarly pushed its first expected cut to December 2026. For IE industrial brokers, the 'higher for longer' rate environment (Fed funds at 3.50–3.75%) will continue to suppress investment sales volume, widen bid-ask spreads on industrial assets, and delay lease decisions by tenants sensitive to financing costs.

articles.headline: BofA and Goldman Push Back Fed Rate-Cut Expectations on Inflation Risks, Jobs Data
articles.source: Wall Street Journal (via Reuters/WHBL citing WSJ-reported data)
articles.summary: A broad coalition of global brokerages — including BofA, Goldman Sachs, and JP Morgan — have revised their Fed rate-cut forecasts significantly later, with BofA expecting no cuts in 2026 and Goldman eyeing December 2026 at the earliest. The 10-week-old Iran war has pushed energy prices higher and U.S. unemployment held steady at 4.3% in April. Traders are now pricing in mid-to-late 2027 for the next Fed cut, according to the CME FedWatch Tool. For IE brokers, this 'rates on hold' environment means industrial cap rates are unlikely to compress near-term, keeping transaction volumes suppressed and making it harder to close investment sales at seller-expected pricing.

articles.headline: JLL Arranges $26M Bridge Financing for Anaheim Industrial Outdoor Storage Facility
articles.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged $26 million in non-recourse, three-year floating-rate bridge financing for a 7.75-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) facility at 1477 N. Jefferson St. in Anaheim, Orange County, on behalf of borrower North Palisade Partners. Senior Director Peter Thompson led the transaction for the Class A, 337,590-square-foot property. The deal reflects continued lender appetite for IOS assets in infill Orange County locations, even in a high-rate environment. For IE and OC brokers, the IOS sector remains one of the most liquid and in-demand industrial sub-types, with strong rent premiums in supply-constrained infill markets like Anaheim.

articles.headline: Top Industrial Leases Recognized for Orange County — Q1 2026 Power Broker Awards
articles.summary: CoStar recognized the top Q1 2026 industrial leases in Orange County, with prominent deals signed by Houdini, Cubework, and Dot Corp., negotiated by dealmakers from CBRE, Prologis, and Tierra West Advisors. The Power Broker Awards highlight the strongest quarterly deal activity evaluated by CoStar's research team across all Orange County industrial transactions. These recognized leases signal continued active deal-making in OC despite rising vacancy (approximately 5.5%) and softening asking rents (down 3.7% QoQ to ~$1.55 NNN/SF/month per CBRE's Q1 figures). For OC industrial brokers, Cubework's presence on the list also signals continued flex/co-warehousing demand in the county.

articles.headline: Commercial Mortgage Volume Rises 52% Year-Over-Year in Q1 2026
articles.summary: The Mortgage Bankers Association reported that commercial and multifamily mortgage originations surged 52% year-over-year in Q1 2026, with industrial property loan originations specifically rising 56% YoY — the fourth-largest gain among property types. The growth was led by an 80% rise in depository lending driven by maturing bank-held loans, and investor-driven lenders posted a 133% YoY surge. While Q1 originations fell 30% sequentially from Q4 2025 (typical seasonal pattern), the annual trajectory is constructive. For IE/SoCal industrial brokers, this data confirms lenders are returning to the industrial sector, which could support more transaction activity in H2 2026 if rate conditions stabilize.

articles.headline: Larger Deals Provide Boost to Orange County's Industrial Market
articles.summary: GlobeSt reported that Orange County's industrial leasing market is showing signs of recovery, with larger deals driving activity to its strongest pace since pre-pandemic levels according to a recent market report. The article notes stable interest rates and resilient consumer demand as key drivers supporting Southern California industrial growth. Orange County industrial availability sits near 5.5%, with asking rents around $18.90/SF annually — among the highest in the nation. For OC industrial brokers, the return of large-format deal activity is a positive leading indicator, suggesting institutional and national tenants are re-engaging with the market after a period of caution.

articles.headline: Recovery Shapes in San Diego's Industrial Market Amid Economic Shocks
articles.summary: San Diego's industrial market posted 220,000 SF of positive net absorption in Q1 2026, pushing vacancy down 20 bps QoQ to 7.7%, driven by move-ins from logistics and consumer goods sectors. North County showed positive signs with moderating availability after two consecutive years of new-leasing growth, while Otay Mesa saw elevated vacancy at 15.7% due to large tenant move-outs, though it remained one of the most active deal submarkets for renewals. The limited development pipeline and strong renewal activity provided supply-side support for stabilization. For San Diego industrial brokers, the market is diverging sharply by submarket — Otay Mesa offers value-add and large-block opportunities, while North County commands premium rents from life sciences and defense-adjacent users.

articles.headline: California Ports Show Resiliency, With Long Beach Setting Record for TEUs
articles.summary: A Savills research report highlighted that the Ports of LA and Long Beach combined to handle more than 20 million TEUs in 2025 — both ports' busiest years on record — despite April-June tariff-driven volume dips. The Port of LA handled 10.2 million TEUs in 2025 (its 26th consecutive year as the top U.S. container port), while Long Beach set its own TEU record. Critically, neither port experienced meaningful congestion or extended vessel wait times, a sharp contrast to prior disruption cycles. For IE industrial brokers, record port throughput underpins the long-term demand thesis for Inland Empire warehouse and distribution space, even as current vacancy remains elevated due to the construction overhang.

articles.headline: Inland Empire Industrial Vacancy Rate Increased to 8.9% in Q1 2026 — Cushman & Wakefield MarketBeat
articles.summary: Cushman & Wakefield's Q1 2026 Inland Empire MarketBeat reported the overall vacancy rate at 8.9% (up 10 bps QoQ, up 40 bps YoY), while the strictly industrial vacancy rate reached 8.5% — 50 bps above Q4 2025 and well above the 10-year average of 4.0%. The report noted that peak vacancy may be approaching as the construction pipeline dwindles sharply. National conditions are improving with vacancy dropping below its 2025 peak, while West Coast markets continue to lag on occupancy declines. For IE industrial brokers, the data confirms the market remains in a tenant-favorable environment with negotiating leverage, but the pipeline's collapse signals conditions for rent recovery as early as late 2026 or 2027.

articles.headline: AI Is Now the Leading Driver of Change in Corporate Real Estate, Survey Finds
articles.summary: New research from CoreNet Global and Colliers found that 51% of more than 1,000 corporate real estate professionals surveyed at recent global summits identified AI and automation as the most significant force shaping CRE operations — surpassing sustainability, portfolio optimization, and workforce changes. The findings reflect a growing shift toward AI-driven warehouse management, predictive analytics for space utilization, and robotic fulfillment systems that are reshaping the physical requirements of industrial facilities. For Inland Empire and SoCal industrial brokers, this trend accelerates demand for modern, automation-ready facilities with high power capacity (3,000+ amps), reinforced floors, and tall clear heights — features that older Class B/C warehouse stock in the IE cannot easily provide.

articles.headline: Hot CPI Report Likely to Put Fed on Guard for Longer-Lasting Inflation; Rate Hike Odds Rising
articles.summary: April's hotter-than-expected CPI reading of 3.8% — up from 3.3% in March — is likely to put the Fed on alert that high energy prices are feeding through into broader consumer prices. According to CME FedWatch, markets are pricing in a nearly 98% chance the Fed holds rates steady at its June meeting and through most of 2026. Economists including RSM's Joe Brusuelas stated 'we're not getting rate cuts this year,' while Morgan Stanley's Ellen Zentner noted the data reinforces that new Fed leadership won't bring an immediate dovish shift. The odds of a rate hike in 2026, while still below 50%, are described as 'rising' by Morningstar's Preston Caldwell.

articles.headline: BofA Delays Fed Rate-Cut Forecast Into 2027
articles.summary: Bank of America Global Research has revised its Federal Reserve rate-cut forecast, now expecting the Fed to hold rates steady through all of 2026, with two quarter-point cuts delayed until July and September 2027. BofA cited elevated inflation driven by energy prices from the Iran conflict and a stronger-than-expected labor market, with nonfarm payrolls rising 115,000 in April and unemployment holding at 4.3%. The Fed held its benchmark rate at 3.50%-3.75% at its April 29 meeting in an unusually divisive 8-4 vote, the closest since 1992. Headline PCE accelerated to 3.5% year-over-year in March while core PCE rose to 3.2%.

articles.headline: Columbia Container Lines Signs 68-Month, $13.6M Lease for 156,096-SF Industrial in Fullerton
articles.summary: Columbia Container Lines LAX, Inc. signed a 68-month lease for a 156,096-square-foot industrial property at 691-701 Burning Tree Rd. in Fullerton, Orange County, valued at more than $13.6 million. The Klabin Company/CORFAC International represented Columbia Container Lines, with Tyler Rollema, SIOR, and Matt Stringfellow, SIOR, leading the transaction. The company is relocating and expanding from its prior location as part of the deal. The landlord was not disclosed in the available details.

articles.headline: CoStar: U.S. Industrial Vacancy Remains in Mid-7% Range Entering Q2 2026, Expected to Edge Higher Into 2027
articles.summary: CoStar's revised forecast shows the national industrial vacancy rate remaining in the mid-7% range entering Q2 2026 and expected to edge higher into 2027 before beginning a gradual descent. West Coast port markets, despite facing lower new supply risk, are set to continue underperforming due to reduced demand, with availability in large, newer logistics properties near major West Coast ports exceeding 13%, compared to about 9% for East Coast ports. The ongoing trade disruptions weigh heavily on port markets exposed to Chinese trade, while improving demand in the latter half of 2026 may offer some relief, potentially returning national rent growth by 2027. Inland Empire, Los Angeles, and San Jose are expected to continue negative absorption into early 2027.

articles.headline: JLL Capital Markets Arranges $26M in Bridge Financing for Anaheim Industrial Outdoor Storage Facility
articles.summary: JLL Capital Markets arranged $26 million in bridge financing for a 7.75-acre industrial outdoor storage (IOS) facility located at 1477 N. Jefferson St. in Anaheim, California. Senior Director Peter Thompson, Associate Kyle White, and Analyst Nick Englhard worked on behalf of borrower North Palisade Partners to secure a non-recourse, three-year, floating-rate loan. The Class A property encompasses 337,590 square feet. Specific loan terms and the lender were not disclosed in the announcement.

articles.headline: Columbia Container Lines Leases 156,096 SF Industrial Property in Fullerton
articles.summary: The Klabin Company/CORFAC International represented Columbia Container Lines LAX, Inc. in a 68-month lease for a 156,096-square-foot industrial property at 691-701 Burning Tree Road in Fullerton, Orange County. The lease is valued at more than $13.6 million. Tyler Rollema, SIOR, and Matt Stringfellow, SIOR of The Klabin Company represented the tenant, which is relocating and expanding from a prior location. The landlord's representation was not disclosed in the announcement.
